title: Anticipation effects in DID: pre-announced policy

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Event Study approach to test for anticipation effects in DID. I'll estimate period-specific treatment effects relative to the announcement (period 3) and implementation (period 5) to detect pre-emptive responses. Key assumptions: (1) parallel trends would hold absent treatment, (2) no other confounding events, (3) anticipation effects, if present, should manifest between announcement and implementation periods.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(dplyr)
library(fixest)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s10_data.csv")

# Create period dummies and interaction terms for event study
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    # Create relative time periods (relative to announcement in period 3)
    rel_time = period - 3,
    # Create treatment x period interactions for event study
    treat_x_period_1 = treated * (period == 1),
    treat_x_period_2 = treated * (period == 2),
    treat_x_period_3 = treated * (period == 3), # announcement
    treat_x_period_4 = treated * (period == 4), # between announcement and implementation
    treat_x_period_5 = treated * (period == 5), # implementation
    treat_x_period_6 = treated * (period == 6),
    treat_x_period_7 = treated * (period == 7),
    treat_x_period_8 = treated * (period == 8)
  )

# Event study regression (omit period 2 as base period, just before announcement)
event_study <- feols(y ~ treat_x_period_1 + treat_x_period_3 + treat_x_period_4 + 
                     treat_x_period_5 + treat_x_period_6 + treat_x_period_7 + 
                     treat_x_period_8 | unit_id + period, data = data)

print("=== EVENT STUDY RESULTS ===")
print("Testing for anticipation effects between announcement (period 3) and implementation (period 5)")
print(summary(event_study))

# Extract key coefficients
coef_announce <- coef(event_study)["treat_x_period_3"]
coef_anticipation <- coef(event_study)["treat_x_period_4"] 
coef_implementation <- coef(event_study)["treat_x_period_5"]

print("\n=== KEY FINDINGS ===")
cat("Announcement effect (period 3):", round(coef_announce, 4), "\n")
cat("Anticipation effect (period 4):", round(coef_anticipation, 4), "\n")
cat("Implementation effect (period 5):", round(coef_implementation, 4), "\n")

# Test for anticipation: is period 4 coefficient significantly different from 0?
anticipation_pvalue <- summary(event_study)$coeftable["treat_x_period_4", "Pr(>|t|)"]
cat("P-value for anticipation effect:", round(anticipation_pvalue, 4), "\n")

# Standard DID for comparison (ignoring anticipation)
standard_did <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = data)
print("\n=== STANDARD DID (ignoring anticipation) ===")
print(summary(standard_did))

# Robustness: DID with announcement variable
did_with_announce <- feols(y ~ treat_x_announce + treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = data)
print("\n=== DID WITH ANNOUNCEMENT VARIABLE ===")
print(summary(did_with_announce))

# Create summary of results
cat("\n=== SUMMARY OF ANTICIPATION ANALYSIS ===\n")
if(anticipation_pvalue < 0.05) {
  cat("FINDING: Significant anticipation effects detected (p < 0.05)\n")
  cat("Banks appear to pre-emptively adjust capital ratios after announcement\n")
} else {
  cat("FINDING: No significant anticipation effects detected (p >= 0.05)\n")
}

cat("Standard DID coefficient:", round(coef(standard_did)["treat_x_post"], 4), "\n")
cat("This", ifelse(anticipation_pvalue < 0.05, "may be biased", "appears unbiased"), 
    "due to", ifelse(anticipation_pvalue < 0.05, "presence", "absence"), "of anticipation effects\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect positive anticipation effects (coefficient ~0.1-0.3) for treated banks in period 4, indicating they pre-emptively raise capital ratios between announcement and implementation. This would suggest banks respond proactively to regulatory announcements, violating standard DID assumptions and potentially biasing the treatment effect estimate downward if anticipation effects are ignored.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: DID with anticipation — must account for pre-announcement window; use period ≤2 as clean pre-period
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Constrained banks raise capital ratios both after announcement and after effective date
